name: Otis Worldwide Corporation

profile.description: Otis Worldwide Corporation is the world's largest elevator and escalator manufacturing, installation and service company, operating through New Equipment and Service segments. Founded in 1853 by Elisha Otis, inventor of the safety elevator, it was spun off from United Technologies (now RTX) in April 2020 and is headquartered in Farmington, Connecticut. FY2025 net sales were $14.43B with net income of $1.38B [2]. Q3 2026 net sales rose 6% to $3.9B (organic +6%), with Service up 8%, New Equipment up 3%, modernization backlog up 20%, and GAAP EPS up 14% to $1.08 while adjusted EPS was flat at $1.05 [3]. In September 2026 Otis announced CEO Judy Marks will retire once a successor is named, expected in the first half of 2027 [7].

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Otis has layered a digital service business onto a 170-year-old mechanical franchise through its Otis ONE connected-elevator platform for predictive maintenance, and has turned modernization into its fastest-growing line — Service modernization sales rose 20% and modernization backlog grew 20% in Q3 2026 [3][8]. AI Deployment (1/2): Marks describes the operating model as 'human-led and AI-enabled' and Otis is rolling out AI-driven pricing in service [5][8], but management has slowed that rollout to protect customer retention and has not quantified AI savings. Market Share (2/2): Otis is the largest of the global 'Big Four' elevator OEMs with the industry's largest service portfolio, producing a 24.2% Service operating margin in Q3 2026 [3]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Modernization orders up 10% at constant currency and New Equipment backlog up 4% give revenue visibility [3], but no named next-generation products with launch dates were found. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D of $152M was about 1.1% of 2025 sales [2], typical for industrial machinery.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): Otis's purpose — to give people freedom to connect and thrive in a taller, faster, smarter world — connects the business to urbanisation and human mobility, and the board credits Marks with embodying the 'Otis Absolutes' of safety, ethics and quality that drive the culture [7]. Community Impact (1/2): Otis publishes ESG goals and Sustainalytics rates its ESG risk low at 18.8, ranking it 29th of 577 machinery companies [9][10]; general rather than distinctive community programs. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data was found, though Marks publicly values a unionised workforce united with management around customers and service quality [6]. Insider Buying (0/2): FMP data show no open-market insider purchases and periodic insider sales in 2025-2026 [12].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Dividend stock (12 weight units). Otis has negative shareholders' equity (book value of -$14.26 per share) from its spin-off capital structure and buybacks, so D/E and ROE are undefined and both are scored at the floor (0.0) [1]. Quarterly revenue growth of 6.1% YoY scores 0.87, while the 5-year revenue CAGR of 2.5% ($12.76B in 2020 to $14.43B in 2025) scores 0.50 [1][2]. Forward P/E of 16.9 beats the 20x target (1.0) and profit margin of 10.3% scores 0.51 [1]. Dividend metrics: payout ratio 42.8% (0.95), 7 consecutive years paid since the 2020 spin-off (0.70, 2x weight), 6 consecutive annual increases (0.60), and a derived 5-year dividend CAGR of 12.9% from the $0.24 quarterly rate in 2021 to $0.44 in 2026 (1.0, 2x weight) [1][11]. Weighted sum 7.84/12 = 6.53, rounded to 7. Liquidity: 4.24M avg volume × $75.75 = ~$322M daily.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Otis's revenue comes from manufacturing, installing, modernising and physically maintaining elevators and escalators under strict safety codes — work performed by unionised technicians on a vast installed base that AI cannot substitute [3][6]. Analysts see the bigger near-term risk as execution on AI-driven pricing and cost programs rather than disruption, and data-centre and urban construction add demand for vertical transport [8]. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI is used internally (pricing, Otis ONE predictive maintenance) under a 'human-led and AI-enabled' model [5], but Otis reports no quantifiable AI-attributed revenue.

infinite_game.summary: Otis carries one of the longest-lived causes in industry — making vertical movement safe since Elisha Otis's 1853 safety brake — and its 'Otis Absolutes' culture of safety, ethics and quality gives it real staying power [7]. Sinek would also note finite tendencies: a capital structure with negative equity built on buybacks, about $1.3B returned to shareholders year-to-date in 2026 [3], and an upcoming CEO transition that will test whether the culture outlasts its leader [7].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): The purpose of giving people freedom to connect and thrive in a taller, faster, smarter world is distinctive and rooted in 170 years of safety leadership, and Marks frames the company's cultural Absolutes as the source of its strategy [5][7]. It has not yet been tested through a leadership transition as an independent company — the first will come in 2027 [7].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Marks argues that Otis's culture benefits from management and union labor being united in purpose around customers and service quality [6], and the board describes the succession as a long-standing plan [7]. No turnover or tenure data was found to evidence an exceptionally high-trust organization.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No fetched evidence showed management framing Kone, Schindler or TK Elevator as rivals to learn from; public commentary focuses on Otis's own service portfolio, margins and share of modernization demand [3].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Otis has evolved from a mechanical OEM into a service- and digital-led business with Otis ONE connectivity, and has leaned into modernization as new-equipment markets slowed [3][8]. This is meaningful adaptation within the elevator category rather than a fundamental reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Management slowed the rollout of AI-driven pricing to protect customer retention despite pressure on margins and lowered EPS guidance [8] — a choice of long-term relationships over short-term earnings. Elsewhere, capital allocation leans heavily on buybacks and dividends, with ~$1.3B returned year-to-date in 2026 [3].

investment_thesis: Otis is a high-quality, annuity-like service business: Q3 2026 net sales rose 6% to $3.9B with Service up 8%, Service operating margin of 24.2%, modernization sales up 20% and modernization backlog up 20% as aging elevator fleets are upgraded [3]. GAAP EPS rose 14% to $1.08, year-to-date adjusted free cash flow reached $834M, and the company returned about $1.3B to shareholders [3]. At 16.9x forward earnings with a 2.3% yield, a 42.8% payout and a dividend that has compounded about 13% a year since the spin-off [1][11], Otis offers durable income growth with minimal AI disruption risk.
thesis_continued: The concerns are growth and balance-sheet structure. Revenue has compounded only 2.5% a year since 2020 [2], adjusted EPS was flat in Q3 2026 and adjusted operating profit slipped $6M after the full-year profit outlook was cut in Q2 [3][4], and New Equipment backlog grew just 4% amid weak China construction. Negative shareholders' equity (book value -$14.26/share) with about $8.7B of debt [1] means continued buybacks rely on leverage, and the 2027 CEO succession after Judy Marks's retirement [7] introduces strategic uncertainty.
key_catalysts: Modernization backlog up 20% and modernization orders up 10% at constant currency converting into higher-margin Service revenue through 2027 [3]
Service margin expansion (24.2% in Q3 2026, +100bps sequentially) as AI-enabled pricing and productivity programs mature [3][8]
Naming of a successor CEO in H1 2027 providing strategic clarity and continuity of the Otis Absolutes culture [7]
key_risks: Negative shareholders' equity with ~$8.7B debt leaves less flexibility if service growth slows or rates rise [1]
Prolonged weakness in China and global new-equipment markets (NE backlog only +4%) limiting top-line growth to low-to-mid single digits [3]
CEO transition risk: Judy Marks's retirement in 2027 after leading Otis since before the spin-off [7]

backlog.note: Q3 2026: modernization backlog +20% (actual and constant currency) on modernization orders +10%; New Equipment backlog +4% at constant currency [3]. Absolute backlog dollars and TTM book-to-bill were not found in fetched sources, so the signal reflects strong modernization growth offset by sluggish new-equipment orders.
